title: Zechariah 13:7–9
context: The LORD of Armies calls the sword to awake against my shepherd, the man who is close to me: strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered. Two parts of the land will be cut off, and a third left, refined as silver and tested as gold; they will call on the LORD’s name, he will answer, and he will say, It is my people, and they will say, The LORD is my God (compare Hosea 2:23; Zechariah 8:8). The shepherd’s identity in the oracle is debated; the passage follows the shepherd material of chapter 11, and some connect it with the worthless shepherd of 11:17, while many see a good shepherd close to the LORD. Matthew 26:31 and Mark 14:27 report Jesus citing the line on the night of his arrest as the disciples were about to be scattered (compare Matthew 26:56; Mark 14:50); each Gospel uses it in its own setting, and the wording in both is first person, I will strike the shepherd. Many in both traditions read the oracle in light of the Gospels and of Christ’s suffering under the LORD’s purpose (compare Isaiah 53:10), while holding the details of how the whole oracle is fulfilled with care. Shared ground: Arminian and Reformed readers generally treat the refining of a remnant and the renewed covenant bond as common confession (compare Malachi 3:3; 1 Peter 1:7).

verses.text: “Awake, sword, against my shepherd, and against the man who is close to me,” says the LORD of Armies. “Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered; and I will turn my hand against the little ones.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see the LORD of Armies calling the sword against his shepherd, with the sheep scattered. Many read it in light of Matthew 26:31, where Jesus cites the line on the night of his arrest.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the shepherd close to the LORD struck under God’s purpose, and many read it in light of Mark 14:27 and Isaiah 53:10. Shared ground: both traditions generally hold the details of fulfillment with care.

verses.text: It shall happen that in all the land,” says the LORD, “two parts in it will be cut off and die; but the third will be left in it.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see two parts of the land cut off and a third left. Judgment is severe, yet a remnant remains by God’s mercy.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God preserving a remnant through judgment. Shared ground: both traditions generally read the verse soberly, holding the fractions as poetic language for widespread loss and survival.

verses.text: I will bring the third part into the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will test them like gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will hear them. I will say, ‘It is my people;’ and they will say, ‘The LORD is my God.’ ”
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see the remnant refined like silver and gold, calling on the LORD and answered by him. Trial leads to renewed relationship.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the covenant formula restored, It is my people, and The LORD is my God (compare Hosea 2:23). Shared ground: both traditions generally treat refining and renewal as common confession (compare 1 Peter 1:7).
